thread.title: Cisco, Apple, Netflix lead Silicon Valley stocks higher as Facebook slips on Soros sell-off

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Cisco, Apple, Netflix lead Silicon Valley stocks higher as Facebook slips on Soros sell-off
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 15, 2018, 1:55pm PST Updated Feb 15, 2018, 2:01pm PST Cisco Systems shares reached dot-com era highs on Thursday after the San Jose-based company reported strong earnings. The stock (NASDAQ: CSCO) was the best performer on the Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech index, gaining 4.73 percent on Thursday. Apple Inc (NASDAQ: AAPL) surged 3.36 percent after legendary Warren Buffett doubled down on his stake in the Cupertino-based iPhone maker . While the Berkshire Hathaway chairman famously doesn’t care much for tech stocks, preferring steady investments like Coca-Cola that generate predictable revenue, he’s been loading up on Apple shares in recent years and has praised the company’s consistent profits. Of course, the appetites of billionaire investors can turn both ways. Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) slipped as much as 1.4 percent on Thursday after George Soros ' investment fund sold off its remaining stake in the Menlo Park-based social media platform, per a regulatory filing spotted by CNBC . Facebook shares recovered as the day went on, and closed up slightly, at 0.25 percent. CEO Mark Zuckerberg is also selling off hundreds of millions of dollars of stock in the company to fund his Chan Zuckerberg philanthropic initiative. Soros has called Facebook a "menace," joined a chorus of critics who have condemned social media's role in furthering the spread of fake news, foreign propaganda and violent and obscene content. The Facebook dump came as Soros bought up a large stake in online discount retailer Overstock.com (NASDAQ: OSTK), per CNBC. His fund is now the third-largest investor in Overstock, which has seen its shares surge since announcing in September that it was adding a cryptocurrency trading product. Soros also bought more shares in Facebook competitor Snap Inc (NYSE: SNAP) and Google parent Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ: GOOG), CNBC noted. The Bloomberg index gained 2.49 percent on Thursday. Here's what other Silicon Valley stocks did. Along with Cisco and Apple, other top performers: Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) jumped 5.36 percent, making it the best performer among all Silicon Valley stocks on Thursday, as the stock got a boost from an analyst upgrade and after signing hit producer Ryan Murphy . Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) bounced 3.65 percent. At least one usually bearish analyst has said he thinks the carmaker will hit its Model 3 production targets . Silicon Valley's worst performers on Thursday: Redwood City-based data center owner Equinix (NASDAQ: EQIX) dropped 6.54 percent after it reported Q4 results and said it was spending $800 million in cash and stock on a Dallas data center . NetApp (NASDAQ: NTAP) slumped 4.9 percent on an earnings outlook that hinted at future weakness . SunPower Corp. (NASDAQ: SPWR) slid 1.2 percent after reporting earnings. Barron's explains how President Donald Trump's solar tariffs are hurting SunPower while helping competitor SolarEdge Technologies (NASDAQ: SEDG). GoPro (NASDAQ: GPRO) closed down slightly after surging on Wednesday. CEO Nick Woodman gave an interview earlier this week outlining the company's future after its decision to quit the drone business. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 15, 2018, 1:55pm PST Updated Feb 15, 2018, 2:01pm PST Related Content
